Notes: First documented Jewish resident: Solomon Davidovich (35) a Polish soldier sent to work at the Luhansk foundry
One Jew reported in the settlement at the Luhansk foundry (single individual; count not stated)
Approximately 156 Jews at the foundry settlement itself (153 in nearby Slavyanoserbsk listed separately); source says 1862
Russian 1897 census: 2109 persons of Jewish faith (~20% of population per source); conflicts with 1505 in other source
Three Jewish schools opened in 1910; from 1908-1916 J.B. Lerner was government-appointed rabbi; organized community
More than 7000 Jews (~9% of ~80000 inhabitants); figure is a lower bound
Jews 5% of total per source (as printed)

Germans occupied city 17 July 1942; most Jews evacuated or fled; 1038 remained; majority murdered at Ivanitchev Yar 1 Nov 1942 and 21 Jan 1943 together with Jews from other localities (1986 victims total, not a town population)
Approximately 7800 Jews in the city; community revival from 1992 (cultural center Ner; Hesed Ner)
